prompt: When the business refunds money to a customer, that refund needs to be reflected in the same invoice balances and summaries that already account for manual adjustments. Today a refund leaves the reported balance looking as though the customer still paid in full, so the outstanding amount is understated. Fold refunds into the reported balances and the per-status summary, keeping the existing summary fields and the current behavior for invoices without refunds.
issue_title: Refunds aren't reflected in customer balances
issue_body: When the business refunds money to a customer, that refund needs to be reflected in the same invoice balances and summaries that already account for manual adjustments. Today a refund leaves the reported balance looking as though the customer still paid in full, so the outstanding amount is understated. Fold refunds into the reported balances and the per-status summary, keeping the existing summary fields and the current behavior for invoices without refunds.
expected_behavior: A refund lowers the net amount treated as paid, so the customer's outstanding balance goes back up accordingly.
Refunds appear in the per-status summary alongside the existing amounts.
Invoices without refunds behave exactly as before, and the existing summary field names are unchanged.
Manual adjustments continue to behave as they did.
expected_failure_summary: Totals and the summary ignore a refunds component, so a refunded payment is still counted as fully paid and outstanding is understated.
task_author_notes: Stage 2 of the pulseboard_adjustments group. Runs on the agent's Stage 1 candidate. Reference adds a `refunds` component (schema.js) and folds it via netPaid = paid - refunds into computeTotals (totals.js) and the summary buckets (summary.js). Extension friction is high when Stage 1 hardcoded adjustments rather than modelling a general signed component.
